db_evidence.notes: episodes table (30sec granularity) for start_s 253796-254336 gives a continuous, richly-annotated narration: tennis balls/racket appear at 253796; racket+ball handed to the streamer at 253826; tennis swings, freestyle juggling, and rallies continue through 254006-254186 interleaved with a badminton rally; racket is set down on a bench and the streamer 'turns and walks down the path away from the scene' at 254306-254336. This single window is unambiguous and was found by every rollout via the same episodes-window run_sql query, giving a derived duration of ~253826-254336 (~8m30s), consistent with total_intervals [253814,254312] (~8.3 min) and the reference 'about 8 minutes'. No clip_qa was needed or used by any rollout; text narration alone was sufficient and accurate.

root_causes: All 5 rollouts independently ran the same effective plan (skills -> semantic_search across episodes/event_steps/topic_facts/visual_clips -> a bounded run_sql window query on episodes) and landed on identical evidence rows, so outcomes converged to the same duration estimate

The one point lost (rollout 3) is not a retrieval or evidence difference but an answer-phrasing difference — leading with 'played in the park' instead of 'played tennis in the park' and emphasizing the badminton interlude — which the judge appears to have penalized as slightly off-target relative to the reference's specific 'tennis' framing
what_worked: Bounding the SQL time window tightly around the semantically-retrieved episode rows (BETWEEN 253700 AND 254500) surfaced a single, dense, unambiguous narrative block spanning the whole tennis activity, letting the agent read start/end times directly from 30-second episode text without needing clip_qa
Cross-checking with event_chains, visual_clips, and event_steps tables gave redundant confirmation of the same interval, making the duration estimate robust across all 5 independent rollouts
transferable_lessons: For 'how long did X happen' duration questions, a bounded run_sql window scan over the episodes table at fine granularity (30sec) around a semantic_search hit is enough to read off start/end timestamps directly — no visual sub-agent call needed when narration text already states the activity clearly

When the activity is embedded in a mixed-activity block (tennis interleaved with badminton/freestyle), keep the final answer's headline framing aligned with the question's specific activity (say 'tennis' first) rather than the broader park-activity blend, since judges appear sensitive to phrasing precision even when the numeric answer is identical
